newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq eases after two sessions of gains.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq eases after two sessions of gains.

text.p: Selling knocked the top off technology stocks on Tuesday after two sessions of record gains. Blue-chip tech stocks on the Nasdaq suffered even sharper losses than their small-cap counterparts on the index.
The Nasdaq Composite finished unofficially down nearly 11 points, or 0.82 percent to 1328. The top 100 stocks fell nearly 18 points, or 1.92 percent, to 915.
The losses followed increases on Friday and Monday, when the Nasdaq composite index posted its first and second largest single-day gains, respectively.

"The market was ripe for profit-taking, and in fact held together pretty well considering the run-up," said Robert Baird and Co's head of equity trading, Barry Berman. "It's really all technical in nature right now unless you see really big volume or a big disparity in the advance/decline line."

Despite the loss, the number of stocks that gained on Tuesday was greater than the number of stocks that fell, 2228 to 2108 with 1094 stocks unchanged. However, the volume of falling shares that traded beat advancing volume four to three.
Intel Corp shares closed down 4-1/2 to 158, hurt by reports of a possible bug in its new Pentium chip that could cause computational errors in rare cases.

Cisco Systems Inc shares closed down 1-1/8 to 57-3/4. After the close the company reported earnings per share of $0.52 for the third quarter, excluding a gain of $0.03 a share. The result was in line with analysts' expectations for earnings of $0.52 a share, according to First Call consensus estimates.

Duramed Pharmaceuticals fell 5-1/8 to 5-1/4. Yesterday the FDA said it would not approve at this time a generic version of the estrogen replacement drug Premarin. Duramed has had an application for generic conjugated estrogens pending since September, 1994.
